title: Completeness as operadic localization
statement: Let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal and use [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. The complete objects of $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ are exactly the objects local for the single map $s:E^1\to E^0$. The localization at the strongly saturated class generated by $s$ has as its inverted maps exactly the fully faithful and essentially surjective maps; its unit $A\to LA$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Here strongly saturated means closed under equivalences, two-out-of-three, retracts, pushouts and small colimits of arrows. If $\mathcal V$ is symmetric monoidal, its algebroid tensor $A\otimes B=\mu_*(A\boxtimes B)$ of [lem-coef-algebroid-external-product] carries a fully faithful essentially surjective map tensored with any identity to another such map. The map $A\otimes s$ is a local equivalence for every algebroid $A$. Thus completion is compatible with this tensor and the complete-object tensor is $L(A\otimes B)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2, Theorem 5.6.6, Proposition 5.5.9 and Proposition 5.7.14; monoidal localization in Corollary 5.7.15 Read online where available; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$, which is presentable by [lem-coef-algebroid-presentability]. The current definition [def-coef-complete-algebroid] defines completeness by $I_0(A)\to I(A)$ being an equivalence, where $I_n(A)=\operatorname{Map}(E^n,A)$ and $I(A)=|I_\bullet(A)|$. By [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve], $I_\bullet(A)$ is a groupoid object. The effectiveness statement in [lem-coef-space-geometric-descent] identifies $I_1(A)$ with $I_0(A)\times_{I(A)}I_0(A)$ and makes $I_0(A)\to I(A)$ surjective on $\pi_0$. Under this identification the degeneracy $I_0(A)\to I_1(A)$ is the diagonal. An equivalence $I_0(A)\to I(A)$ has an equivalence as diagonal. Conversely, if the diagonal is an equivalence, then each homotopy fiber of $I_0(A)\to I(A)$ is nonempty and its diagonal is an equivalence. For any two points in such a fiber, the space of paths between them is a fiber of that diagonal and therefore contractible. The fiber is thus contractible. Hence $I_0(A)\to I(A)$ is an equivalence. This proves that complete algebroids are exactly the objects local for $s:E^1\to E^0$.

Apply [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] to the singleton $\{s\}$ to obtain a reflector $L$ onto the full subcategory of complete algebroids. By [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation], its inverted class $W$ is the strongly saturated closure of $s$, detected by mapping into complete algebroids, and every unit lies in $W$.

Use [lem-coef-algebroid-categorical-homotopy] to form the coherent simplicial algebroid $D_n=A^{E^n_{\mathcal S}}$. All its structure maps and the augmentation maps $A=A^{E^0}\to D_n$ are categorical equivalences: they are cotensors of maps between the nonempty finite indiscrete space-enriched algebroids. Hence they are fully faithful, essentially surjective, and induce equivalences on maps into every complete object. The detector in [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] puts these maps in $W$. Let $\widehat A=|D_\bullet|$, which exists by presentability. The augmentation gives $j_A:A\to\widehat A$ in $W$: it is the colimit of the arrows $A\to D_n$. The colimit of the constant $A$-diagram over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $A$, because $[0]$ is initial in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, so its nerve is contractible; equivalently mapping out gives the limit of a constant mapping space over a contractible index. This identifies the source of the colimit arrow, and $W$ is closed under small arrow-colimits. The construction and $j_A$ are functorial in $A$.

source.place: Definition 5.6.1 and Theorem 5.6.2, first proof paragraph

proof.text: All structure maps of $D_\bullet$ are fully faithful, so [lem-coef-algebroid-ff-simplicial-realization] makes $j_A:D_0\to\widehat A$ fully faithful and identifies $U(\widehat A)$ with $|U(D_\bullet)|$. By [lem-coef-space-geometric-descent], $U(D_0)\to|U(D_\bullet)|$ is surjective on $\pi_0$. In particular every object of $\widehat A$ is joined by a path in its object space to an image object, and hence is equivalent to one; thus $j_A$ is essentially surjective by the objectwise criterion in [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve]. The cotensor identity identifies $U(D_n)$ with $I_n(A)=\operatorname{Map}(E^n,A)$, so $U(\widehat A)\simeq I(A)$.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, proof, essential surjectivity and the Segal-presheaf argument

proof.text:
We prove completeness of $\widehat A$ rather than assume that realization commutes with $\operatorname{Map}(E^1,-)$. Use the notation $I_n,I$ of [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve]. There is a commutative square with top row $|I_0(D_\bullet)|\to I_0(\widehat A)$ and bottom row $|I_1(D_\bullet)|\to I_1(\widehat A)$; vertical maps insert identity equivalences. The top row is an equivalence by [lem-coef-algebroid-ff-simplicial-realization]. The left vertical map is also an equivalence: cotensor adjunction and symmetry of products of space-enriched algebroids identify $I_1(A^{E^n})\simeq I_n(A^{E^1})$, naturally in $n$. Under these identifications the left vertical map is $I(A)\to I(A^{E^1})$ induced by $A\to A^{E^1}$. This map is a categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-algebroid-categorical-homotopy], hence fully faithful essentially surjective, and its $I$-map is an equivalence by [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve].

To verify the bottom row, each map $D_m\to D_n$ induces an equivalence $I(D_m)\to I(D_n)$. Effectiveness of their equivalence nerves identifies $I_1(D_k)$ with $U(D_k)\times_{I(D_k)}U(D_k)$. Therefore the naturality squares of $I_1(D_\bullet)\to U(D_\bullet)^2$ are pullbacks. Cartesian geometric descent and preservation of finite products from [lem-coef-space-geometric-descent] give a pullback square $I_1(A)\to|I_1(D_\bullet)|$ over $U(A)^2\to U(\widehat A)^2$. On fibers over $(x,y)\in U(A)^2$, its top map is an equivalence; so is $I_1(A)_{x,y}\to I_1(\widehat A)_{j_Ax,j_Ay}$, since $j_A$ is fully faithful by step 3 and the nerve lemma preserves these fibers. Two-out-of-three makes the comparison $|I_1(D_\bullet)|\to I_1(\widehat A)$ an equivalence on those fibers. The map $U(A)^2\to U(\widehat A)^2$ is surjective on $\pi_0$ by step 3, so the fiberwise detection clause of geometric descent proves the comparison an equivalence everywhere. Three sides of the first square are now equivalences, so $I_0(\widehat A)\to I_1(\widehat A)$ is an equivalence. By the equivalence proved in step 1, this is completeness in the current equivalence-nerve-realization definition.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, proof, completeness square and cartesian descent

proof.text: Since $j_A\in W$ and $\widehat A$ is complete, it exhibits $\widehat A$ as $LA$: for complete $Z$, restriction along $j_A$ is an equivalence of mapping spaces, by the detector of [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation]. This is the reflector's mapping-space universal property. The resulting natural comparison $LA\simeq\widehat A$ identifies the unit with $j_A$. Consequently each unit is fully faithful and essentially surjective by step 3.

First check two-out-of-three for fully faithful essentially surjective maps, using [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve]. For $A\xrightarrow{F}B\xrightarrow{G}C$, if $F,G$ have the property, their composite is fully faithful and its $I$-map is a composite of equivalences, hence it is essentially surjective. If $G,GF$ have the property, full faithfulness of $F$ follows by cancellation on mapping objects, and $I(F)$ is an equivalence by cancellation; therefore $F$ is essentially surjective. If $F,GF$ have the property, cancellation gives $I(G)$ an equivalence, hence essential surjectivity of $G$. For $b,b'\in B$ choose equivalences $Fa\simeq b$ and $Fa'\simeq b'$ using essential surjectivity of $F$. Conjugating by them identifies the mapping-object map for $G$ at $(b,b')$ with its map at $(Fa,Fa')$. The latter is an equivalence by cancellation between the mapping-object maps for $F$ and $GF$. Composition with the chosen object equivalences induces equivalences of mapping objects by the nerve lemma. Thus $G$ is fully faithful as well.

For $f:A\to B$, consider its natural square with units $A\to LA$, $B\to LB$. Its vertical maps have the property by step 5 and belong to $W$ by step 1. Two-out-of-three in each class reduces both questions about $f$ to the corresponding questions about $Lf:LA\to LB$. Between complete objects, a fully faithful essentially surjective map has an equivalence on $I$ and thus on $U$, so is an algebroid equivalence by [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve]. Conversely an equivalence has both properties by their definitions. A map between local objects lies in $W$ precisely when it is an equivalence, by [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] and the fact that the reflector is identity there. Thus $f\in W$ if and only if it is fully faithful and essentially surjective.

Now suppose $\mathcal V$ is symmetric monoidal. By [lem-coef-algebroid-external-product], the object space of $A\otimes B$ is $U(A)\times U(B)$ and its mapping objects are $A(a,a')\otimes B(b,b')$. For fully faithful $f:A\to A'$ and any $B$, the mapping-object maps of $f\otimes1_B$ are $f_{a,a'}\otimes1$, hence equivalences since tensor is a functor. If $f$ is essentially surjective and $(a',b)$ is a target object, choose $a$ and an equivalence $fa\simeq a'$. Tensor its unit-valued forward and inverse morphisms with $1_b$; their compositions are the identity by the tensor's compatibility with composition and units. They give an equivalence $(fa,b)\simeq(a',b)$. Thus $f\otimes1_B$ is also essentially surjective. For $1_B\otimes f$, its mapping-object maps are $1\otimes f_{a,a\prime}$ and are equivalences. For a target object $(b,a\prime)$ choose $a$ and inverse equivalences $\alpha:fa\to a\prime$, $\beta:a\prime\to fa$. The morphisms $1_b\otimes\alpha$ and $1_b\otimes\beta$ connect $(b,fa)$ and $(b,a\prime)$, and their composites are identities by compatibility of tensor with composition and units. This proves essential surjectivity in the other factor as well. These are arguments from the stated tensor and the definition of equivalence; no theorem about an underlying functor preserving arbitrary limits is used. Here the passage between essential surjectivity and the existence of image objects up to equivalence, and the interpretation of these unit-valued inverse morphisms as equivalences, are exactly the objectwise and invertible-component clauses of [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve].

source.place: Proposition 5.7.14, explicit mapping objects and object equivalences

proof.text: Since $W$ is the strongly saturated class generated by $s:E^1\to E^0$, one has $s\in W$. Step 6 shows that $s$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Step 7 then gives the same properties for $1_A\otimes s$ for every $A$, and step 6 again puts this map in $W$. Thus $A\otimes s$ is a local equivalence, without presuming that completion commutes with tensor.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.9 in the symmetric-monoidal case; alternatively Proposition 5.7.14 after Corollary 5.6.3

proof.text: The coherent symmetric tensor on all algebroids is supplied by [lem-coef-algebroid-external-product]. By steps 6 and 7 its inverted class $W$ is stable under tensoring on either side. It contains equivalences and is closed under composition by step 1, so apply [lem-coef-relative-symmetric-monoidal-localization] to $(\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V),W)$. It gives a coherent symmetric monoidal localization with $L(A)\otimes L(B)\simeq L(A\otimes B)$. The reflector $L$ of step 1 also has the functor-category localization property: writing $i$ for the full inclusion of complete objects, any functor $F$ inverting $W$ has a natural equivalence $F\xrightarrow{F\eta}FiL$, since every unit $\eta$ belongs to $W$. Conversely $L$ inverts $W$, and $Li\simeq1$. Restriction along $L$ and precomposition with $i$ are therefore inverse on the corresponding full functor infinity categories; their natural units give these identifications also on transformations and higher coherences. Consequently the underlying localization identifies with the full subcategory of complete objects. Transfer this tensor along that equivalence. For already complete $A,B$, its value is $L(A\otimes B)$, with the coherent associativity, symmetry and unit constraints of the cited localization theorem. This is the required compatible completion tensor.
